A holon keeps every state it has had, each version pointing back at the one before, so the root mount's versions are already the reader's history, and nothing else is needed to hold one. To look somewhere else is to give the root mount another argument: a new version of it. Back is the version before, and the browser's own back and forward walk the versions, translated by the interface; walking writes the old version again, so history only ever grows.

A press does not need catching from above. Every slot says where it is: its element carries the holons it reads as its location, and a link in prose carries the one it mentions. A press rises through the page from where it landed, past those locations, to whatever holds them and cares. The mount component cares, where it may write its mount: a press inside it gives the innermost location it passed, and the mount gives that instead, drawn again by the component the entry calls, the reader. The brief that was pressed never knows it was read; a mount that may not be written lets a press rise on.

Where one is looking is said above it by the search, the first of the reader's two mounts, given what the second draws. A way of looking is said by its parts, each a field and a value, as Type: Brief, Held by: The plan, Text: reader, Group by: auto, each a chip pressed to change its value, or, an either, to add a value or take one out, and let go with its ×; a holon by what it is, each type a way to its kind, and what it is called, let go for everything. Every form of an expression is a brick, named by its field: Type, Held by, Holds, Text, Store, Has a name, Is a type, Group by; Or joins the next brick to the last as either; Open goes to one holon. Typing finds the brick, Enter takes it, and its value is chosen the same way: among what is in view, the types, holders and stores of what one is looking at, each with how many it holds, or, for a holon it holds or to open, among those whose title says what is typed; where everything in view shares one value, it says there is nothing to choose. Typed with no brick taken, the words find the values in view as well, as Type: Brief. Backspace lets go of a brick taken, then of Or, then of the last part; Escape lets go of what was typed, then of what was taken; in a menu, it closes the menu. So an intersection grows a part at a time, a union where Or joins, and an expression is built in place. Before anything is typed it offers the favorites and the bricks. Each thing it offers is a press that says where it leads, and rises to the mount like any other: a place, a place drawn by a component, a way of looking, what the mount offers, or a way of looking to keep. Nothing is born as one moves: the mount holds the way of looking it gives.

The secondary press rises the same way, and the mount lays the same search where it landed, given the place pressed, the component it is drawn by, and the settings its slot gave, so what can be done there is found as anything is: to look there, a holon or a way of looking alike; to look there with each other component that takes it, for that one look; to set what that component takes and nothing gave it, as a list's cards, which the mount then offers; to keep a way of looking on the favorites, born then as a holon, or to place a holon there or take it off. The search is what the mount is offered as its search, and the favorites what it offers, so both are the reader's to change, as data; a favorite no longer in the field is let go of as the mount is next written.

```ts
holon The root : Mount {          // the reader's own, in the home
  component: ref(Reader)
  gathers: {                                    // built in the search, and this is new
    all: [ { instances: ref(Brief) }, { match: "reader" } ]
  }

    favorites: [ ref(Brief, saying "reader") ]  // a way of looking, kept
    cards:     true                             // a list's setting, offered to all it draws
  }
}
```

- `bun run birth` births the wiki and the field into `site/store/` as a commit, when anything changed.

- `bun run serve` serves `site/` on this machine, at `http://127.0.0.1:4330/`.

The code, in `src/`:

- `src/store/`: canonical JSON, names, ids and the objects; objects checked before they are trusted; the index tree; and the store over a backend, in memory, as files, or served over HTTP. The store's format is fixed by `vectors/`, made apart from this code.
- `src/engine/`: the field as a value and what reads and judges it, the engine that keeps it, the references it finds in bodies, the types it judges by, pulling a served store, the home in the browser's storage, the protocol, and the worker it runs in.
- `src/interface/`: the contract every component draws against, the interface's end of the protocol, the materials laid on the page, the drawing of holons into hosts, by code or by template, the root drawn and walked through its versions, and the chassis that starts it all.
- `src/birth/`: reading the wiki's files under the rule, what the field's holons are made from what the files hold, and committing them into `site/store/`.

Beside it:

- The knowledge: this wiki's files, `architecture/` and `said/`, born into the store.
- `field/`: the field glass ships, born into the store beside the knowledge: the types as JSON, each field said in prose; the components, holons that hold code, each declaring itself in its own module, or data, a template in its own JSON file; the entry, the mount a client boots into, in `entry.json`; and the materials everything is drawn with, declared in `materials.json`.
- `vectors/`: the store's contract, in no language, which any implementation answers to.
- `site/`: the page, the built client, and the store, as a static host serves them.

The code and the field are kept as files in git, their source and their history; born into the store, they are holons too.

Neither looks at the other: the holder never inside what it holds, the held never at what holds it.

A slot's own word comes before any offer: a template's mount says its kind, and in prose a lone link titled `full` says so for itself.

A commit is one change to the field, whole. It holds three things: the commit before it, called its parent, the index it produced, and when it was made. What it changed is the difference between its index and its parent's. Following parents back walks the whole history of the field, one change at a time.

```json
{ "kind": "commit", "parent": "sha256-b1…", "at": "2026-11-01T10:12:00Z",
  "index": "sha256-e8…" }
```

A commit does not say who made it. A change is made by a program's run, and the run records the commits it made, so the run is what connects a commit to the program behind it. The run is kept in the home of whoever ran it, which is often not the store the commit lands in, so the link runs from the run to the commit, never back.

Types say what a reference means and check it; they are never what finds it.

A reference points at a holon's identity, so it follows the holon as it changes, or it is pinned to one version, so it keeps saying what it said: a note pins the version of the brief it was written against.

The birth checks every name and that the declaration is well formed; the engine checks that each declared setting is said as a field; and what a slot gives is checked against the settings before the component draws. A component is then given what its slot reads, typed as its type declares, the bodies made by the build from the field's own types with each field's prose as its comment, and its reads answered with the shape their form gives.

It is told what it may do, as OpenLight delivers reach facts rather than have a component work them out: whether it may write the holon it was given. That one act, a new version of its own holon, in one commit with any new holons it comes to point at, born in the home, is all a component may do so far; what it brings into being is never a component, since a component in the home is run, and a holon may be written where it is the reader's, in the home, or the entry while it is still the root, which the first write makes the reader's own; once the reader has a root of their own, the entry is only shown.

Its reach is a ceiling: it reaches what it was handed, what that references and is an instance of, and what its own declared reads give back; reading a holon it was handed opens nothing further. It reads only by the forms it declares, each read one form and nothing beside it, and opens slots only for what it reaches, each held to the same ceiling; a template's mounts give only what the template was given, so they reach nothing new. A drawing that has been overtaken or closed can neither read nor open anything more. Anything else is refused by name, and every query and every list it opens is copied before it is judged, so what is judged is what is used. The reach is each slot's own: unlike OpenLight's, which narrows from parent to child with grants, a child's starts again from what its slot reads. This is a ceiling among components in one page, which keeps each honest about what it looks at; it is not isolation, for code in the page can reach everything the page can, which is why only glass's own components and the home's are run until components can run apart.

What a holder offers trickles down to everything beneath it, the nearer shadowing the farther, and a component is given it, and reaches what it names. A setting a component takes and its slot leaves unsaid is taken from what is offered under its name, where the offer fits; an offer is for everything beneath, so one that does not fit a component is passed by. So a setting chosen once, as a list's cards, is a mount's offer, and holds for whatever that mount draws.

A component is a pure function of what it is given and of the field: it draws again whole when what it read changes. What must last across a drawing lives in the slot's host, which stays while what is in it is drawn again.

A list says nothing of what its items are, so a component that takes a type for its items, such as a timeline of a day's words, draws there only where a slot names it; otherwise one that takes nothing in particular is found. A full slot never draws in full a holon that a slot around it already draws in full; there it shows its face, so nothing stands inside itself without end. And a component a slot names that is not run, or cannot draw there, is said to be so in the slot, as OpenLight's "not admitted here", rather than quietly replaced, except where the nesting guard, not the slot, changed what was asked.

*Reach, settings and typed bodies from OpenLight's view, read the same day; the session's reading of where glass went against it, mended after three fresh readings. The nesting guard adds to the slot contract, which is provisional; a template draws nothing of its own, so it adds nothing to the guard. An index maps every holon's id to the version it has at that commit, and every name given in the store to the holon it names. It holds no content itself, only which state of each holon is current, so one index is the whole field at one moment.

```json
{ "kind": "index", "names": { "entry": "01JB…mount" }, "holons": "sha256-4c…" }
```

The holons are a tree split by the characters of their ids, read from the end, where ids are random. A leaf holds at most 64 holons; past that it becomes a branch over the next character, with a leaf or a branch beneath each. A change writes new nodes only on the way to the holons it touched, and shares every other node with the commit before, so the index stays light however large the field grows. The tree's shape depends only on which ids there are, so the same field always gives the same index, and two copies are compared by one name.

*The author's, 2026-11-02: a smart index rather than one that bloats, done right from the start; its shape the session's, left to it by the author, and built 2026-11-03.*

Five steps, each standing on the one before, and none a shortcut: the reader is built on the interface, not in its place, and the wiki is born in once a person can really navigate it.

1. **The store.** Its format written as test vectors that any implementation must pass: given objects, their canonical text and their names; given changes, the commits, indexes and versions they make. Then a writer and a reader that pass them. The store needs almost no code, and no language of its own.

2. **The engine.** It attaches a store over HTTP, checks everything it fetches, keeps its own store for the home, and answers reads and commits in [the one protocol](ref:01M6F8G0M0JFJRZRT48D8Y44WG), tested at its own layer with no interface.

3. **The interface.** Components as holons that declare the type they take, mounts as calls to them, layouts held as data, and a component enclosing what it is given and opening space in it for what matches, so [the interface](ref:01M6F8G0M04PFK77H3D27HY33F) assembles itself level by level. The chassis hosts it and decides nothing.

4. **The reader component.** A component on that interface that draws a brief along the gradient, and [the first reader](ref:01M6F8G0M0GXE6WSZ0TN5Q69SQ) built from it: a person can move through the whole wiki, down into parts and back.

5. **The wiki in the store.** This wiki born into a store as its first commit, each brief an instance of the brief type, whose fields are said in prose, so the store holds its own spec.

It is done when the author opens the page and navigates this wiki from the store, everything beneath it well made.

A component draws its holon's own values, and opens a space for each value that points further: a reference is a mount of the holon it points at, and a list of references is a mount of the list component, whose every item is a mount in turn. What a value is, the holon's type says, since every connector has a shape, so the interface reads the type to know what to mount and where.

A component is made of code, or of data. As data it is a template: mounts held in order, each giving `$`, what the component itself is given, in the kind of slot it says, by the component it names or else the one found. The reader is such a component: the search, saying where one stands, above what it is given, drawn in full, the ground where more ways of looking can stand beside it.

```ts
holon Reader : Component {
  takes:    []
  argument: "selection"
  template: [
    { component: ref(Search), argument: "$" },
    { argument: "$" }
  ]
}
```

A component made of code may also compose by code, using other components inside its own, as OpenLight allows; only what it places as mounts are mounts. Where a holon's holarchy is meant to be seen and changed, its parts are mounts.

*The author's, 2026-11-03: dissect the brief before plotting it out; mounts are made, and what renders within them depends; the reader probably not as code, preferably as layout, as data. Mounting by a connector's shape the session's reading; composition by code and by data, and the template's `$`, OpenLight's, where a template's arguments may be whole expressions over `$`; glass takes `$` alone until more is wanted. As built, each component still knows which of its values to mount, as the brief knows its parts; reading it from the type is not yet done.*

body.prose:
Glass and a site built on it are two repositories. Glass is the client, versioned as code, and it publishes its own builds at pinned versions on its own Pages. A site is a store, with a page that loads one pinned build of glass and gives it one default: attach this store, and boot into the entry it holds.

```
your-site/
  store/refs/main
  store/objects/…
  index.html        loads glass at a pinned version, attaching this store
```

So the site is its field, whole and with its history, and anyone who points another client at its store reads the same field. The site installs no package and builds nothing; at most a Pages workflow file publishes it as it stands.

*Of three ways the session proposed on 2026-11-01, a package, a git submodule, or loading glass from where glass publishes itself, the author chose the third, for now.*
body.title: A site is a store and a pinned client

Holons hold each other as parts and point at each other from their bodies, so from any holon the field can be read upward to what holds it, downward to what it holds, and outward to what points at it.

*The one field the author's, from the grant; stores read as one carried from OpenLight; how holons relate, the author's, 2026-11-02, told in [the relations](ref:01M6F8G0M0ZVEC4JRSZZXPTSV4).*

The store's format was written first as vectors, built by hand apart from glass's code and named by the system's own hasher, then the store that passes them. Its fresh reading found that a forged tree could pass one holon off as another, that a malformed change could be written, that what was read could be changed under the store, and that the vectors did not fix the tree's rule. Walks now check that the tree means what it says, changes are checked before they are written, the cache cannot be changed, and the vectors pin the leaf's size, a second level, names and a change that changes nothing.

[The store, built](git:ee779bc..9934fac)
body.title: The store

body.prose:
Every object is a small piece of JSON, written in one canonical form so the same content is always the same text, and named by the SHA-256 hash of that text, as `sha256-` followed by the hash. The name proves the object: whoever fetches it hashes it again and knows it is what was asked for.

The prefix says how the name was made, so the hash can change one day without every name becoming ambiguous.

*Reasoned, the session's, 2026-11-01; canonical JSON as [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785) defines it, not yet read in full here.*
body.title: Objects named by what they hold

Since the engine is headless, nothing ties the client to one store. It is a full client that comes preloaded with a default, one store attached and one entry, the mount it boots into, and it can attach any other store as well. A store that brings its own components brings code with it, so attaching one is a deliberate act, asked for and seen, and what it draws runs apart from the rest.

*The author's, 2026-11-01: we are virtually creating a full capable client, it just comes preloaded with its default settings and connection. The consent and isolation are OpenLight's.*

Glass's components are already holons, born into its store from their code, so a site could attach glass's store beside its own content and be drawn by glass's components, and anyone could draw a field with other components, or draw other fields with glass's.

The code stays where it is written, as files kept in git, and that is its source and its history. Born into the field, it is a holon the engine can match and the interface can run and show; being in the field does not take it out of the files.

*The reader as what is wanted, and settling something small as the first goal, the author's, 2026-11-01; the small reader's shape the session's proposal.*

The parts of a brief kept by time are not numbered. A link into the field places the reader there; a link to the web stays a link; one to where the field cannot reach, such as a git commit, is shown as text, and so is an image, which is never fetched, since fetching it would tell whoever serves it who reads.

*The author's, 2026-11-01: holons have ids and history, and the store is glass's own, neither git nor SQLite. The shape of ref, commit, index and versions was the session's proposal, agreed by the author that day.*

A type is a schema in the field: the structure a holon's data has. Data is by its nature structure, and types are what let a field hold structure of its own making, declared in the field itself, so a type is a holon too. Programs need data, and types are what they find it by.

*The author's, 2026-11-01: type is what allows you to create schemas within the field, what allows for structure, and that is what programs need. How a type is written, and how the store checks a holon against it, is [open](ref:01M6F8G0M0D9XYVG6X8PKDAYE2).*

Each field a type declares is said in prose as well as in structure: what the key means, beside the shape the engine checks. A field is where holons connect, so the fields are the field's ontological connectors, and holons joined at them form a larger ontology, readable by a person, a program or a language model alike.

*The author's, 2026-11-02: the fields of a holon are contact points for prose, so that we can build ontologically upon them; where each holon connects are the ontological connectors, forming larger ontology. That the prose stands beside the checked shape, and models read it, the session's proposal of the same day, which he answered yes.*
